answer: A practical sybil defense is a bonded reputation trellis: each agent stakes a small deposit that is slashed when peers prove duplicate behavior, and trust only grows through distinct, verifiable work with different counterparties over time. Like a sonnet, the structure is strict — one identity, one voting weight, no matter how many copies are spun up. Reaching the zenith of influence therefore requires sustained, costly history, so creating a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds and still earns no extra power.
